title: 한눈에 ①: 왜 늦었어요? 이유·원인 표현 구별하기
objective: By the end, you can choose between -아/어서, -(으)니까, -느라고, -기에, -(으)므로, -는 탓에 and -는 바람에, based on the subject, the type of sentence (command, apology, written notice) and the kind of result.
summary: A one-page comparison of seven Korean ways to give a reason or cause, with the key limit of each one.

task.title: Choose and fix reasons
task.line: Read each sentence, check the subject, the verb type and what comes after, then choose, fill in or correct the reason form.

forms.when: Most common, neutral reason. Also used in thanks and apologies. Can't come before a command (-(으)세요) or suggestion (-(으)ㅂ시다). No past tense before it.
forms.exampleMeaning: My stomach hurt, so I went to the hospital.

forms.when: A reason you give to the listener. Fine before commands and suggestions.
forms.exampleMeaning: The roads are jammed, so let's take the subway.

forms.when: Doing A took my time, so B didn't happen. Same subject in both parts, action verbs only, no past tense before it. The result is usually bad.
forms.exampleMeaning: I was playing games, so I couldn't do my homework.

forms.when: Something I saw or heard led me to act. The second part is usually my own action. Not before commands. A little formal.
forms.exampleMeaning: The sky looked cloudy, so I took an umbrella.

forms.when: Formal reason in writing: notices, reports, essays, announcements.
forms.exampleMeaning: This road is dangerous, so please drive slowly.

forms.when: Blaming a cause for a bad result.
forms.exampleMeaning: I missed the train because I overslept.

forms.when: A sudden or unexpected event caused the result (usually bad). The second part is in the past tense. The subjects can be different.
forms.example: 갑자기 비가 오는 바람에 옷이 다 젖었어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: It suddenly rained, so my clothes got all wet.

watchOut: 비가 와서 우산을 가져가세요 (X) → 비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요 (O): -아/어서 can't come before a command or a suggestion.
늦었으니까 죄송합니다 (X) → 늦어서 죄송합니다 (O): for thanks and apologies, use -아/어서.
동생이 떠드느라고 제가 못 잤어요 (X) → 동생이 떠드는 바람에 제가 못 잤어요 (O): -느라고 needs the same subject in both parts.
바쁘느라고 (X) → 바빠서 (O): -느라고 goes only with action verbs, not adjectives.
친구를 만났느라고 (X) → 친구를 만나느라고 (O): no past tense before -느라고. The second part shows the time.
exercises: Choose the right form: ① 날씨가 (추워서 / 추우니까) 따뜻하게 입고 나가세요. ② (도와주셔서 / 도와주시니까) 정말 감사합니다.
Fill in with -느라고 or -는 바람에: ① 저는 보고서를 쓰____ 점심을 못 먹었어요. ② 옆집 개가 밤새 짖____ 한숨도 못 잤어요.
Find and fix the one mistake: 요즘 피곤하느라고 운동을 못 해요.
This is a notice in an apartment building. Choose the form that fits a written notice: 내일 물탱크 청소가 있(어서 / 으므로) 오전에는 물이 나오지 않습니다.
Fill in the blank with -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 (마시다): 어제 커피를 너무 많이 ____ 잠이 안 왔어요.
Fill in the blank with -기에 (싸다): 시장에서 사과가 ____ 한 상자 샀어요.
